sections.name: File setup, REPORT_REASONS
sections.title: Allowed report reasons
sections.what: Lists the four reasons a report may use: abuse, spam, impersonation and other. Users choose one from this list.
sections.why: A fixed list keeps reports consistent for owners to read.
sections.watch_out: Adding a reason means updating every place that shows reasons.

sections.name: reportInput, ReportInput, transferInput, ReportDTO
sections.title: Report input rules and owner view
sections.what: Validates a report's user id, reason and optional note, with friendly messages for a bad reason and for a note over 280 characters. Also defines the transfer input and the report shape owners see.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the friendly messages.
sections.watch_out: The transfer input and the note limit are not enforced when the service is called directly.

summary: Defines the allowed report reasons and the shape of a report, with the checks on report input.
purpose: Makes sure report input is valid and gives owners a defined report shape to read.
why: Likely reason: one shared check so every report follows the same rules.
how: 1. Lists the four reasons. 2. Requires a user id, a valid reason with a clear message, and an optional trimmed note of 280 characters or fewer. 3. Defines a transfer input with a user id. 4. Defines the report shape owners see.
outputs: Validated report data, or messages explaining what is wrong.
risks: The transfer input is defined but the moderation service takes a plain id, so this check is not used by the visible code. The note limit only applies when input passes through the schema.
debug: If a report is rejected, read the message: it names the reason or the note length. If a long note was saved, check whether the caller skipped the schema.
